records.segregation: Linkage to 6q24 by homozygosity mapping; homozygous deletion in affected children
quotes: We performed genome-wide homozygosity mapping in a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with five children affected with FHL.
By screening positional candidate genes, we identified a homozygous deletion of 5 bp in the syntaxin 11 gene (STX11) in this family.

quotes: Of 32 patients from Turkey, 14 had mutations in PRF1, six had mutations in UNC13D, and six had mutations in STX11.
We identified mutations in 38 samples (20 in PRF1, 12 in UNC13D, and six in STX11).

phenotypes.text: onset below 3 months of age (Trp374X carriers)

quotes: The mutation Trp374X in PRF1 was found in 12 patients from Turkey and was associated with a very early onset of the disease below the age of 3 months in all cases.
three of 23 and four of 23 patients from Germany, and three of eight and two of eight from other origins showed mutations in PRF1 and UNC13D, respectively

records.label: Six STX11-mutated FHL patients from 4 PRF1-negative families

phenotypes.text: long disease-free remissions (>=1 year) without specific treatment
myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myelogenous leukaemia

quotes: Two different STX11 mutations were identified, one nonsense mutation and one deletion, affecting six of 34 children in four of 28 unrelated PRF1 negative families.
Three patients experienced long periods (> or = 1 year) in remission without specific treatment, which is very uncommon in this disease.
Two of the six patients harbouring STX11 gene defects developed myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or acute myelogenous leukaemia (AML).

records.label: Patient A
records.segregation: Parents heterozygous for the STX11 mutation and unaffected
quotes: Sequencing of the coding regions and splice-sites of UNC13D, STX11, and STXBP2 revealed that all three patients were homozygous for a novel STX11 mutation, c.173T > C (p.L58P) (Table 1).

In addition, patient A was heterozygous for a rare UNC13D c.811C > T (p.P271S; frequency 0.001 in a Caucasian population of 4294 individuals) variant inherited from the father and homozygous for an uncommon UNC13D c.2782C > T
it is possible that the UNC13D variants contribute to the severity of disease presentation in patient A.

records.label: Patient B

phenotypes.text: Deficient NK cell activity and degranulation

quotes: Here, we describe two infants and one 5-year-old child born to unrelated Pakistani families that presented with HLH (Table 1).
The parents were heterozygous for this STX11 mutation, but did not have any recorded history of inflammatory disease.

records.label: Patient C

phenotypes.text: Deficient NK cell activity and degranulation
Greatly reduced syntaxin-11 expression in PBMC and LAK cells

quotes: Patient C also presented with a hyperinflammatory syndrome and was later referred to the Aga Khan Hospital.
Stx11 levels were found to be greatly reduced in the patient (Figure 3A).
LAK cells from the patient also displayed a selective loss of Stx11 expression, whereas Munc18-2 expression was similar to that of control LAK cells (Figure 3B).

notes.statement: In an open-label, single-group phase 2-3 study, Locatelli et al. (2020) gave emapalumab, a human anti-interferon-gamma antibody, with dexamethasone to 34 patients aged 18 years or younger with primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (27 previously treated, 7 previously untreated). Of the previously treated patients, 63% had a response, compared with a prespecified null hypothesis of 40%. Seventy percent of them proceeded to transplantation, and 74% were alive at the last observation.
quotes: a total of 34 patients (27 previously treated patients and 7 previously untreated patients) had received emapalumab; 26 patients completed the study.

A total of 63% of the previously treated patients and 65% of the patients who received an emapalumab infusion had a response; these percentages were significantly higher than the prespecified null hypothesis of 40% (P = 0.02 and P = 0.005, respectively).
In the previously treated group, 70% of the patients were able to proceed to transplantation, as were 65% of the patients who received emapalumab.

notes.statement: Locatelli et al. (2020) found that emapalumab was not associated with any organ toxicity. Severe infections developed in 10 patients during treatment, and emapalumab was stopped in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.
quotes: Emapalumab was not associated with any organ toxicity. Severe infections developed in 10 patients during emapalumab treatment. Emapalumab was discontinued in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.

notes.statement: Müller et al. (2014) identified a homozygous STX11 c.173T-C (L58P) missense mutation in the Habc domain in 3 children with FHL4 from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families. The parents were heterozygous and had no history of inflammatory disease.
quotes: We identified a homozygous STX11 mutation, c.173T > C (p.L58P), in three patients presenting clinically with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis from unrelated Pakistani families.
The parents were heterozygous for this STX11 mutation, but did not have any recorded history of inflammatory disease.

notes.statement: Müller et al. (2014) found defective NK cell cytotoxicity and degranulation in patients homozygous for STX11 L58P; IL-2 stimulation partly restored both. Perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a expression was normal.
quotes: All patients displayed defective lysis of K562 target cells and degranulation by NK cells in response to K562 target cells or engagement of the Fc receptor CD16 (Figures 1A,B). Notably, cytotoxicity and degranulation were partially restored by IL-2 stimulation (Figures 1C,D).
expression of cytotoxic granule constituents’ perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a was normal in patient NK cells

notes.statement: Müller et al. (2014) found that in HEK-293T cells the syntaxin-11 L58P and N-peptide R4A mutants were expressed at wildtype levels but did not bind Munc18-2. In contrast, the C-terminal Q268X FHL4 mutant still bound Munc18-2. The authors proposed that loss of Munc18-2 binding may destabilize syntaxin-11, which would explain its low expression in patient cells.
quotes: In transfection experiments, both Stx11 R4A and L58P mutants were expressed at levels comparable to Stx11 wild-type (Figure 4D).

neither FLAG-tagged Stx11 R4A nor L58P mutants bound HA-tagged Munc18-2 (Figure 4E). In contrast, the C-terminal Stx11 Q268X mutation previously associated with FHL4, did not display impaired binding of Munc18-2 (Figure 4E).
it is tenable that Stx11 mutations that disrupt Munc18-2 binding might reduce Stx11 expression through a similar mechanism, explaining the low expression of mutant Stx11 in patient cells.

notes.statement: Rudd et al. (2006) sequenced STX11 in 28 FHL families without perforin mutations and found STX11 mutations (one nonsense mutation and one deletion, both previously reported) in 4 families (14% of the PRF1-negative families), affecting 6 of 34 children.
quotes: Mutational analysis of STX11 by direct sequencing was done in 28 FHL families that did not harbour perforin mutations
STX11 gene mutations were found in 14% of the PRF1 negative FHL families included in the present cohort.

notes.statement: Rudd et al. (2006) concluded that STX11 mutations were associated with a milder phenotype with prolonged remissions without specific treatment, but that some patients developed severe psychomotor retardation, and suggested that STX11 mutations may be associated with secondary malignancies (MDS/AML).
quotes: Despite the milder phenotype, some children with STX11 mutations developed severe psychomotor retardation.

These results suggest that STX11 gene mutations may be associated with secondary malignancies (MDS/AML), and that there is segregation of specific clinical features in FHL patients with an underlying genotype.

notes.statement: Zur Stadt et al. (2006) screened 63 unrelated FHL patients and found STX11 mutations in 6 of the 32 patients from Turkey. They found no STX11 mutations among the 23 German patients or the 8 patients of other origins. FHL2, FHL3, and FHL4 together accounted for 80% of HLH cases of Turkish origin and 30% of German cases.
quotes: Of 32 patients from Turkey, 14 had mutations in PRF1, six had mutations in UNC13D, and six had mutations in STX11.
but none in STX11. Thus, FHL-2, FHL-3, and FHL-4 account for 80% of the HLH cases of Turkish origin, and for 30% of German patients.

notes.statement: Zur Stadt et al. (2006) concluded that FHL shows extensive genetic and allelic heterogeneity. They found mutations in PRF1, UNC13D, or STX11 in 38 of 63 unrelated patients.
quotes: Our findings demonstrate extensive genetic and allelic heterogeneity in FHL

notes.statement: By genome-wide homozygosity mapping in a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with 5 children affected with FHL, zur Stadt et al. (2005) found linkage to a 10-cM region on chromosome 6q24 between D6S1569 and D6S960, defining a novel FHL locus.
quotes: Linkage to a 10 cM region on chromosome 6q24 between D6S1569 and D6S960 defined a novel FHL locus.

notes.statement: zur Stadt et al. (2005) demonstrated that syntaxin 11 protein was absent in the mononuclear cell fraction of patients homozygous for the 5-bp STX11 deletion.
quotes: We could demonstrate that syntaxin 11 protein was absent in the mononuclear cell fraction of patients with the homozygous 5 bp deletion.

notes.statement: Because both STX11 and UNC13D are involved in vesicle trafficking and membrane fusion, zur Stadt et al. (2005) concluded that, besides perforin mutations, defects in the endocytotic or exocytotic pathway may be a common mechanism in FHL.
quotes: As both STX11 and UNC13D are involved in vesicle trafficking and membrane fusion, we conclude that, besides mutations in perforin 1, defects in the endocytotic or the exocytotic pathway may be a common mechanism in FHL.
